text:
Predicates:
AllowedToMoveIn(x, y) ::: x is allowed to move in with y.
PetsAllowed(b) ::: pets are allowed in building b.
Deposit(b, d) ::: deposit in building b is d.
Rent(b, r) ::: rent in building b is r.
CanBeEqualOrMore(d1, d2) ::: deposit can be equal or more than rent.
Fluffy ::: Tom's cat.
Cat(x) ::: x is a cat.
Pet(x) ::: x is a pet.
ManagedBuilding(b) ::: b is a managed building.
OliveGarden ::: the Olive Garden.
Rent(b, r) ::: rent in building b is r.
Premises:
PetsAllowed(oliveGarden) ::: Pets are allowed in the Olive Garden.
Rent(oliveGarden, 2000) ::: The monthly rent at the Olive Garden is $2000.
2000 > 1500 ::: $2000 is more than $1500.
AllowedToMoveIn(x, y) ← PetsAllowed(b) ∧ Pet(y) ∧ AllowedToMoveIn(x, y) ::: If a managed building allows pets, then people are allowed to move in with a pet.
Tom will rent an apartment in a managed building if he is allowed to move in with Fluffy, and the security deposit is no more than $1500. (This premise is represented as a condition in the conclusion question)
Conclusion:
AllowedToMoveIn(tom, fluffy) ::: Tom is allowed to move into an apartment in The Olive Garden with Fluffy.
